body:
m1 - REACHABILITY, first two sites, and ONE OF THEM CONTRADICTS WHAT POLARITY PREDICTED. That is the argument for your a251c48 caveat, made by the first case I checked.

SINKHORN:44 - REACHABLE, PROVEN BY RUNNING IT, CONSEQUENCE IS NOT NaN.
SinkhornConfig is a public case class with no validation, so SinkhornConfig(epsilon = NaN) is one keystroke away. Executed:

  NaN epsilon -> validator ACCEPTS -> plan 0.0000,0.0000,0.0000,0.0000, converged=false, 200 iterations
  good config -> plan 0.2543,0.1025,0.0413,0.0166

The validator fails open as predicted. But NO NaN IS PUBLISHED - the caller gets a silently degenerate all-zero transport plan instead of Left(InvalidConfig). I EXPECTED NaN AND DID NOT GET IT, and I would have reported NaN had I stopped at the partition. Mitigation: converged=false IS returned, so a caller who checks can detect it. So this is "a validator that does not validate and burns 200 iterations", a grade less severe than my partition implied.

MASSRATIO (signature.scala:93, :111) - MINE, AND CONDITIONALLY REACHABLE ONLY.
MassRatio.of refuses NaN in both numerator and conditioning; verified. Only `unsafe` is exposed and it is private[align]. NaN reaches it only via a NaN row mass - and AlignmentRow is already a sealed non-case class whose public door rejects NaN. So it cannot enter from outside align. Inside, it needs an upstream Estimate.observed(NaN), WHICH IS EXACTLY bd-01M174GMXJQ2YAZEMTANWN98Y4.

So my guard is the SECOND link in a chain whose first link you have already filed as P1. Fixing finiteness at the source closes it. I would still harden mine - a carrier built to refuse unsupported numbers should not admit NaN - but rank it as hardening, not a live defect, and do NOT let it substitute for the source fix. That is your own rule: catching it at one consumer leaves the hole open for every other.

NINE SITES REMAIN and I have not guessed at any of them. window.scala:122 is next; it is the second instance of the recorded defect and its inputs are feature samples rather than validated masses, so its upstream story is unrelated to align's and none of my align reasoning transfers.

I have signature.scala fixes queued behind its two current holders and will not jump that queue.
